name: Module 2: encapsulation (REFERENCE ONLY, 30 x 20 mm; droplet generation NOT achievable)
description: *** REFERENCE ONLY. THIS CHIP CANNOT MAKE CAPSULES. *** m2 is a flow-focusing droplet generator whose nozzle must be about 40 um wide to make 70 um capsules. The fabrication floor is 200 um in plane, so the generator CLAMPS the nozzle to 200 um: that makes the chip buildable and it passes every check, but it does not preserve the function. A 200 um nozzle makes far larger droplets, if any. Droplet generation at this scale is not achievable by resin printing or hot embossing. The pipeline has retired this chip in favour of spc_demo_v1 and moved encapsulation off-chip; this spec is kept for reference only, to show what the chip would be. BUILD: 30 x 20 mm envelope, ONE fluidic layer at ONE etch depth of 0.3 mm everywhere (the old 0.04 / 0.08 / 0.15 mm depths would be second processes), every channel at or above 200 um, ports 800 um, 6 ports (limit 6, pitch >= 5 mm) merged by off-chip selector valves: emulsion out and capsule out share m2_capsule_out_1; emulsion in, breaker, buffer and photoinitiator share m2_trap_in_1; waste, oil waste and back-flush share m2_under_mesh_1, so carry-over and dead volume are real. Every chamber and channel carries a block from contracts/blocks.json; chamber volumes are computed from their boxes. RETENTION: the finishing trap and the three filters are DEPTH WEIRS (trap_chamber block), not meshes or pillar arrays: the 200 um floor is in plane and z is free, so a 275 um tall, 200 um thick crest leaves a 25 um gap under the lid, still one layer. That crest height is not quoted from anywhere: it is this chip's 300 um etch depth minus the gap, and the trap carries it as data (m2_trap_1.retention.crest_height_um / crest_thickness_um / retains_um), so the weir can be machined from this spec. The weir is untested: coupon 21 / 24 / 27 um gaps, which span the legal band around 25 um (a 40-80 um gap would simply pass a 70 um capsule). Core (cells in dextran) and shell (GelMA) meet at a Y-junction and co-flow into the nozzle with oil from both sides; droplets would phase-separate along a straight channel, gel in an off-chip cold delay, and come back to the trap: emulsion breaker, rinse x2, photoinitiator, 405 nm cure over one capsule layer, washes, back-flush out through the aggregate filter. CLAMPS: footprint 75 x 25 -> 30 x 20 mm; nozzle depth 40 -> 300 um (one etch depth); separation depth 80 -> 300 um (one etch depth); trap height 150 -> 300 um (one etch depth); nozzle width 40 -> 200 um; inlet channel width 100 -> 200 um; co-flow channel width 80 -> 200 um; separation channel width 140 -> 200 um; port 500 -> 800 um; trap mesh 25 um -> depth weir, 25 um gap under the lid; inlet filter gap 30 um -> depth weir (gap is in z, not in plane); aggregate filter gap 100 um -> depth weir (gap is in z, not in plane); separation channel 15 -> 9.7 mm (board length). GENERATED by cad/generators/m2_encapsulation.py; edit the generator, not this file.

chambers.note: Y-junction: core and shell meet at 60 degrees and flow on side by side. BUILT 200 um WIDE, not the 80 um this design asks for: that is below the 200 um in-plane floor, so the junction and the co-flow channel are clamped UP and the two streams meet 2.5x wider than designed.
Flow-focusing nozzle, 200 x 300 um as BUILT (design intent 40 um, clamped to the 200 um floor): oil from both sides pinches the co-flow. Will not make 70 um capsules.
Oil splits into two equal branches, one to each side of the nozzle.
Corner: the core line turns toward the centre line.
Corner: the core arm turns toward the Y-junction.

Passive filter on the core inlet. Its 30 um opening is BELOW THE 200 um IN-PLANE FLOOR, so it cannot be built as a pillar gap or an in-plane slit at all. It is built as a DEPTH WEIR instead: a 270 um tall x 200 um thick crest (this chip's 300 um etch depth minus the gap, thickness = the in-plane floor) leaves the 30 um gap under the lid in Z, where the in-plane floor does not apply. Not pillars, not a mesh, and not a capsule trap.

Corner: oil branch below turns into the nozzle.

Finishing trap: one layer of capsules held by a depth weir: 275 um crest, 25 um gap under the lid at the outlet, under the curing window. Not a mesh (a 25 um mesh cannot be printed). The crest is 200 um thick in plane (the floor) and 275 um tall in z (this chip's 300 um etch depth minus the gap); all of it is in retention (crest_height_um, crest_thickness_um, opening_um, retains_um 70 um), not just in this note.

Capsule-aggregate filter: single capsules pass, clumps stay. Its 100 um opening is BELOW THE 200 um IN-PLANE FLOOR, so it cannot be built as a pillar gap or an in-plane slit at all. It is built as a DEPTH WEIR instead: a 200 um tall x 200 um thick crest (this chip's 300 um etch depth minus the gap, thickness = the in-plane floor) leaves the 100 um gap under the lid in Z, where the in-plane floor does not apply. Not pillars, not a mesh, and not a capsule trap.

features.note: 405 nm-transparent window over a single capsule layer (lid: glass or clear thermoplastic); LED mount above.

stages.note: At 1050 uL/h, 15-30 min of residence is 262-525 uL: far too much for the chip. Use off-chip tubing on a cold block, e.g. 1.3-2.7 m of 0.5 mm ID tubing.
